subject: Post-demo: Integration architect handoff, SDK auth & 5xx repro
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmeops.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: priya.khatri@acmeops.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up from today's demo — staging 5xx while testing embed+rerank

Hey Connor —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Priya and I paired up to run a quick staging integration this afternoon and we ran into intermittent 5xxs when calling the embeddings + reranker flow. We attached a stripped-down copy of the staging logs (acme_staging_logs_20261219.txt) and a sample request payload (repro_payload.json).

What we did:
- Using our infra in us-west-2
- SDK: internal nodejs client v0.9.3 (wraps Redwood REST)
- Auth: API key in Authorization: Bearer header
- Request: batch embeddings (batch_size=64) -> reranker call with top-k 10 using those vectors

Observed behavior: about 1 in 6 requests return 502 or 504 from the Redwood endpoint. When successful, results look good. Error seems correlated with larger batches and higher concurrent requests.

Can someone from the tech side confirm whether this looks like a routing/timeout issue vs payload size or model timeouts? We can join a troubleshooting call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Integrations — AcmeOps
[Attachment: acme_staging_logs_20261219.txt (text)]
[Attachment: repro_payload.json (json)]

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmeops.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 18:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — staging 5xx while testing embed+rerank

Alex / Priya —

Appreciate the quick repro materials. Short recap and proposed next steps:

Recap:
- Goal: reliable embed -> rerank pipeline with production-like throughput.
- Immediate symptom: intermittent 5xx (502/504) in staging correlated with large batches and concurrency.

Quick hypotheses:
1) Upstream routing/backpressure in our inference fleet (timeouts or connection resets under concurrency).
2) Large combined payloads hitting request-size or memory thresholds during batching.
3) SDK-level retry/timeout behavior masking real latencies.

Requested info to speed triage:
- SDK version + any SDK debug logs (you included version, thanks).
- Exact cURL-equivalent of failing request or x-request-id header from one failing call if available.
- Are you pinning to a specific model variant or using model discovery?

Immediate actions from our side:
- Looping in Ben (runtime engineer) and Marissa (solutions) to reproduce and check routing.
- Proposed short tech call: Mon 12/21 10:00am PT — 30m — I’ll send a calendar invite.
- Temporary mitigation: try reducing batch_size to 8-16 and confirm if errors persist; we often see large batch sizes amplify upstream memory pressure.

Ben / Marissa — can you take point on a repro and confirm whether we should route them to a dedicated pool (temporary) or tune timeouts?

Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmeops.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 20:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — staging 5xx while testing embed+rerank

Alex — thanks for the logs and payload. Quick debugging notes / actions you can run to help isolate:

1) Repro cURL (single request) — please run from your staging host and paste the response headers. This helps us see x-request-id and any upstream proxy hints.\n
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d @repro_payload.json \n  --max-time 60 \n  --verbose

2) If you see 502/504, capture the response headers (x-request-id, x-upstream, x-runtime) and the exact body.

3) SDK debug: set REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1 (node env) and re-run the batch; attach the debug log. This will show retry attempts and any client-side timeouts.

Notes from a quick scan of your log: I see several connection resets (upstream reset) and a couple of 504s with blank bodies. That pattern tends to mean an inference worker timed out or OOMed while processing a large batch.

Recommendations while we triage:
- Reduce batch_size to 8, set per-request timeout to 60s, disable automatic client retries (we want to see the raw failure).
- If you need throughput, run multiple concurrent smaller batches in parallel rather than one large batch.
- Consider using the streaming output for generation flows; embeddings do not stream, so they need memory headroom.
- If you can, pin the embedding model to "embedder-v2" (we'll confirm the runtime footprint) and try the request again.

Ben Carter
Runtime Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: none]

From: Priya Khatri <priya.khatri@acmeops.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 07:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — staging 5xx while testing embed+rerank

Hi all —

We ran the cURL you suggested from a staging host and pasted the response headers below (redacted):

HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 07:18:02 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
X-Request-Id: a1b2c3d4e5
X-Upstream: inference-pool-7

Body: { "error": "gateway timeout" }

A few notes from our environment:
- Batch size: 64 (we were stress testing throughput)
- Payload compressed size: ~12.1MB per request (we're using gzip in transport)
- Vector dim: 1536 (embedder-v2)
- Concurrent clients: ~6 parallel workers

We attached the staging logs (acme_staging_logs_20261219.txt). There are also a couple of stack traces showing "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError" on our side when we tried to process the responses, which makes us think the payload sizes back to our service are large.

Question: Does Redwood recommend a max payload size or preferred batching strategy for embeddings + rerank? Also, are there any SDK flags to enable chunked delivery or smaller vectors?

Thanks,
Priya
Platform Engineer — AcmeOps
[Attachment: acme_staging_logs_20261219.txt (text)]

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — Integration architect call & mutual action plan

Thanks for the headers and the log snippet — that x-upstream value is exactly the sort of signal Ben wanted. Proposed mutual action plan before our call Monday: 

1) Immediate mitigations (you try):
   - Reduce batch_size to 8 and re-run the cURL test.
   - Disable client-side retries for the test run so we see raw failure modes.
   - If you must keep 64, spread across more concurrent workers with smaller per-request payloads.

2) Redwood triage (we'll do):
   - Ben will reproduce using your repro_payload.json to confirm whether inference workers hit memory limits under current config.
   - Marissa will prepare a short doc with recommended batching, timeout and routing settings (including when to use Dedicated pools vs hosted).

3) Operational follow-ups:
   - Tech call Mon 12/21 10:00am PT — 30m. Agenda: repro walk-through, reproduce live, quick mitigations, next steps for production rollout. Calendar invite incoming.
   - I'll open a support ticket and link it to the HubSpot deal so we keep procurement and engineering aligned: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2026-147

4) Longer-term: consider using Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantization / routing) if embedding throughput and payload costs become dominant. We can include a quick cost-lift estimate during the next call.

If you can run the reduced-batch test before the call, drop results into the Drive folder and Ben will jump in immediately.

Connor
